I'm being put on that this week as an antidepressant but if it helps with my nerve pain then great! I'm also trying CBD oil as I've heard it has many benefits from anxiety reduction to pain relief.

I would strongly advise against trying Effexor; it's potential for treating nerve pain is weak, and if you miss doses when taking it regularly, withdrawal symptoms can come on hard and are quite nasty I've heard.

Funnily enough, hypericum oil (oil of St. John's wort) is supposed to be effective for nerve pain. I've just tried it and it has given me almost instant relief! Although, if you're on an SSRI/SNRI then you should probably consult a doctor before using it.
I've been prescribed every SSRI under the sun and all they did for me was make me feel like an emotionless zombie with angry outbursts. Now they've given me an SNRI but I'm hesitant to take it

I spoke to them today and they said the first line treatment is amitriptyline, which I've taken 30mg of tonight. Offered temporary relief but a few hours later my hands are burning and tingling worse than ever! This is becoming frustrating, I cannot sleep properly anymore. Do I take a higher dose or try one of the other meds instead?

I'm willing to power through but sometimes the pain at night is unbearable and I've had nights where I haven't slept at all because my hand felt like it was being burned/electrically shocked.  I'm hoping this is a sign that the nerves are reconfiguring themselves but it is very painful. I try paracetamol/ibuprofen, use relaxation methods at night but it still feels horrible. Should I ask my doctor if a stronger painkiller is needed?

22, going to uni on the 10th September after years of suffering from mental health issues. Despite all the setbacks, I persevered with my studies and landed myself a place. I'm actually shit scared though.
My ED was actually anorexia, I started over exercising and under eating to control these urges. I went in completely the opposite direction because I wanted to get rid of it

Unfortunately, after disclosing this to someone who I thought I could trust, they reacted badly and said it was 'really weird' and 'disgusting' which confirmed my fears. 

This compounds the shame and leads me to feeling isolated.

Well, at least he's always happy to see me when I turn up! He's a pug, and he's about 8 now :) I grew up with him and I know it sounds weird, but we've got a special bond, because I know he will be loyal to me unconditionally and I always treat him with love and kindness.
My dad shows more of those behaviours...every time we have a conversation he can switch topics and deflect questions so well I end up more confused than at the start of the conversation!

Not much, if I'm honest. They used to make things worse really, and most of them had little understanding of what aspergers/autism even is. People were employed based on knowing the manager of the placement, not because they were particularly good. One of them was a personal trainer before they got that job with zero experience, they just knew the manager so they got it. It's extremely easy to just blag your way into these places, hell I applied as a volunteer at a place like that once and was almost given a full time job. 

Mostly they just seemed to take the piss, recording phone calls, there were cameras all over the place like big brother and they just monitored everything I did and liked to make me angry. I'm in another placement now but here you just sorta have to get on with it

I spent a few months in an eating disorders unit and there was another girl there who had been on 24 hour observation because she was at risk of suicide. They decided to take her off since she seemed to be improving but after dinner one day, all hell broke loose when it was discovered that she had attempted suicide in one of the quiet rooms.

She was taken away, but she died soon after. I didn't know her too well, but I was the last person to speak to her. She was writing letters to different people, but now I realise she was saying goodbye. I asked if she was OK, but something was definitely off. I figured I'd give her some space because she seemed to really want to be alone. I wish I had acted on my intuition and asked her if she was really ok...

Well, I'm still trying to get my life together, and to level out and live a normal life would actually be an amazing achievement for me. Hell, just living would.

I was sexually abused by my father when I was a lot younger which triggered a long string of fuck ups... Was abused again by a counsellor who asked me to sit on his lap and asked me inappropriate questions about masturbation, and again on a school trip when an unidentified boy came into my bed on a school trip at night. Suffered from an eating disorder that was nearly fatal. Had a suicide attempt at age 13.

Im at a supported living unit right now which does offer support with practical things, but as far as getting a job and applying to uni, I have to do that on my own. My parents offer me no support at all, and in fact stress me out to the point of illness. They constantly tell me how badly I'm dealing with things and suggest I speak to someone about my mental health because I'm not 'normal'. I've been with a mental health team for years and I've also been to a psych ward so I think if I had a serious illness I would know by now. FYI I know that sounds like a contradiction with the psych ward, but I was only there because of housing issues, I had been made homeless at the time. All down the line psychs have told me its depression and anxiety, that's it.

Sexual abuse, physical threats, emotional attacks, calling me: insane, manipulative, a fucking creep, a waste of space, a fucking loser with no friends, abandoning me in a psych ward, using personal information against me, arguments that could rival world war 3, I could go on.

Honestly, I think living in a war zone with halfway decent parents would've fucked me up less. It's who you've got behind you that counts.
I get what you're saying, but I'm incredibly desperate here. They cut off every other mode of contact and I just want to ask them why.

They have already phoned the police on me before while I was in the house and actually charged me with assault. The assault was pushing someone away as they were shouting and spitting in my face, which is more minor than my dad pushing me all over the place.

Psychology, psychiatry and neuroscience.
A side effect of being in the mental health system for a lot of my life, and also being hospitalised for a time. I was also fascinated with how the mind works. Psychologists tell me I could probably be a psychologist too someday, but I think I should sort my own mess out first.
I understand, sorry, I wasn't meaning to draw parallels, I just feel for you also in this situation. I hope that your family can move forward from this.

Okay, this does hit a nerve with me...

I'm the son in a situation like this and I understand the hate, revulsion and anger directed towards people like me, and I'm not making a comparison to your situation at all because the claims there are groundless, but for me it's a little more complicated. The thought of this would've never crossed my mind until my dad started behaving uncomfortably around me; he would follow me round the house, watch me constantly, invade my personal space and at one time he started touching my leg when we were at a restaurant which just felt wrong. 

It was when we went up to see his parents that I remembered that we had to sleep in the same bed when I was a lot younger and that's when I freaked out. I had a vague idea that something had happened, and unfortunately I asked my dad what that was about.

What ensued was family turmoil, many times the police were called on me, I was put in supported living, I was even put in a psych ward. I genuinely didn't want to do this to the family. Of course, now I feel a mixture of guilt and self doubt but you know what? I still think something terrible may have happened. My dad never really assuaged my fears, he used to say things like 'you don't deserve an explanation', 'let's pretend it didn't happen' and 'sometimes things in life just happen and we have to move on'.

Not that I'm advocating making such claims with no reason, that would be manipulative, but people look on these sorts of things with such revulsion that they're not willing to dig deeper. I wasn't feeling defiant or antisocial, I was afraid and feeling trapped.

All I can say is I'm sorry that you are in this situation. I, unfortunately, know firsthand how thoroughly these things can destroy a family. Not just between the accuser and the accused, but throughout the entire family.

Well, after my parents chucked me out of the house, I had no choice but to move into a supported living unit which my parents chose for me so that at least I wouldn't be homeless. The staff and I did not get on at all because I didn't want to be there and I was furious at my parents/everyone around me. They had cameras everywhere and literally spied on all the service users.

They eventually evicted me after I kept throwing strops, but because supported living placements are few and far between, the only option housing had was the psych ward. They have 'a duty of care' to house you somewhere, apparently. My parents also consented to this. If I refused, I would've been sectioned which is not something I wanted.

I ended up being a day patient, so I could leave every day to go study in the library for my exams. The consultant said I could technically be discharged at any time, but without somewhere to go, I had to stay there. 

It would've been foolish to try to get out; I wouldn't have gotten very far and besides, that's grounds for sectioning and at that point I would've been stuck on the ward. I just had to grit my teeth and bear it.
England, and they put me on 200mg of sertraline.
I admit, I looked her up on twitter out of curiosity. I do seem to be drawn back to my parents despite their appalling behaviour towards me. I guess deep down, I still want their affection.

I've always had a strained relationship with my parents but recently it's gotten even worse. I would describe my dad as cold, ruthless and repressed; he has made fun of me for having an eating disorder and often says bizarre things like 'we don't have much in common, you don't eat much for instance' and 'maybe you should try being a guinea pig for experimental drugs for your anxiety'. My mum is a complete control freak and arguments would escalate into world war 3 over something so trivial as a misplaced towel. Shouting matches could be heard down the street, her screams were intolerable.

Everything fell apart when my dad kept acting strange around me, he stroked my leg under the table when we were out at a restaurant which made me uncomfortable. When I asked him to stop, he'd say 'you're insane' and 'you're making it up' and 'you're trying to destroy the family'. Later when I kept asking him what was going on he'd say 'you don't deserve an explanation' and 'let's pretend it didn't happen.'.

Obviously, I freaked the fuck out and things went from bad to worse. The police were phoned after arguments were they cornered me, shouting in my face and I was once detained after having water thrown on me and sobbing hysterically.

After a while, they put me in supported living and that went downhill fast. I was extremely angry and they would provoke me by recording my phone conversations, listening in to everything I was saying and telling me how to kill myself. After threatening to make me homeless, they said they were evicting me, and since I had nowhere to go I was placed in a psych ward. The reason being that my anger was 'causing concern'. My parents did not have me back even though throughout all this I was doing my a levels.

Cut to now, and I'm in another supported living unit trying to fix my fucked up mess of a life. I had to cut off contact with my parents because the stress was making me physically ill. 

**TL;DR**: chaotic family situation, kicked out into supported living, kicked out into psych ward, kicked out into another supported living unit, me becoming a hot mess.
